en: Details unknown.
note: Dragon Centaur V.

en: A forest beast that loves silence. It adores Silent Shells, said to absorb sound and spells, and hoards them around itself. It even hates its own growl, so it sewed its mouth shut. In Berte's heyday, it often fought her over rowdy forest drinking parties.
note: Silent Beast. 'Berte's heyday' = while Berte was still active (genneki).

en: A romantic old demon who dearly loves the night sky. Coming across a marvelous gem called the Moonlight Stone, he reaches the very height of happiness. But then his precious treasure is stolen by an order of knights with a ridiculous name.
note: Lunatic Demon. The knights are the player's party (they name their order in the script).

en: A spirit of the dream world. All who sleep are said to appear in Lukoje's world. On leaving it, that is, on waking, Lukoje erases their memories. But Lukoje sleeps too, and only then, they say, can one bring back memories and things from the dream.

A Demon Duke able to physically absorb and dominate others. That power made Animacie overwhelming, but it all went wrong after teaming with Dromea to snare a certain demon and eating its arm. The body, once easily controlled, began warping out of control.
note: Animacie (gender unknown, no pronoun). Last sentence compressed: 'could no longer control the body as before, and began changing into a chaotic shape'. The 'certain demon' is Shantiba (row 364).

en: A Demon Duke, head of Espel-Dex. He sends his demons to many lands for useful results, aiming at last to "negotiate with the gods." Strong, yet he prefers economic and political battles. Revering his ancestor Pel-Dex, he calls himself the second Pel-Dex.
note: Row is the Espel-Dex monster (its leader). Pel-Dex: new name, hyphen as in Espel-Dex.

en: A Demon Duke known as the Grand Chancellor. With Tsakaro's power, he gathers all kinds of information and trades it with other Demon Dukes: Hilde, Zoze, Ixgoil, Espel-Dex and more. Seen as a danger even by the gods, he rarely stays in one place.
note: Samanbeia. Source uses kare (he). Tsakaro as in the key item Tsakaro's Evil Eye.

en: A Demon Duke called the Lady of Darkness. She can't bear anyone lovelier or more glamorous than herself, and uses any dirty trick to bring them down. A master schemer, she's strong in battle too: her lower half attacks, her upper half casts. No openings.
note: Dromea (row name beri- doromea). 'attacks' = physical attacks.

en: A Demon Duke who rules all cats, and could found a cat kingdom at will. Once just a demon cat, kept by a certain Demon Duke. But she fell into a vile trap, lost both arms and was banished. To avenge her, the cat rose up with the keepsake she left behind.
note: Emperor Harold (no pronoun for Harold). 'she' = the former owner (kanojo), i.e. Shantiba (row 364).

en: A great demon-spirit monument roaming the lands like a ghost, binding many souls in itself. The Path of Souls of the god of Dark Oblivion is flawed: at times souls of the in-between arise as cursed wills. Apasha collects them. Even Demon Dukes shun it.
note: Apasha, the Abyss. 'dai-mareihi' = great demon-spirit monument (new term). Last sentence compressed: 'there is a danger of having your soul taken, so even Demon Dukes are loath to approach'.

en: A dragon worshiped by both the forsaken people and the Kin of Darkness of a small Wasteland. Life was simple but peaceful, until one night it and both their leaders fell into a strange stupor and erased the land. It still regrets that night in anguish.
note: Ixgoil (new name). 'both their leaders' = the people's leader and the Kin of Darkness's leader. 'It is said' hedge on the last sentence dropped for space. haichi = Wasteland(s), as in Elm3.

en: A Demon Duke feared as a War General, as is Velkirios. Likes the strong, but likes the weak who still fight back with all they have even more. Dantarius fought Velkirios many times, and at the cost of a leg cut Velkirios's arms down to their present count.
note: Dantarius, Velkirios, 'War General' (tousho): new terms. No pronoun for Dantarius.

en: Daughter of the Demon Duke Zoze. Since Mirco tied a ribbon on her precious Harz Crystal, she's loved him and dreams of slaying him herself one day. Honest, but very slow. With Zoze's power, no one can stop her antics. No one has ever seen under her skirt.
note: Princess Harz. Compressed: 'she does many troublesome things, but with the power inherited from Zoze no one can stop her: a huge nuisance' -> 'no one can stop her antics'.

en: Homunculus siblings, elder sister Alba and younger brother Berta. Their maker, a famed alchemist, for some reason tried to dispose of them. Now self-aware, they resisted and killed their maker, but their bodies began to crumble. They roam, seeking a home.
note: Antiworld. Alba, Berta: new names. Compressed: 'of a certain land' dropped; 'for some reason' on the crumbling dropped; 'a place they can live, a land to settle in peace' -> 'a home'.

en: A Demon Duke. What he's thinking with those round little eyes is a mystery, but he seems to want to pass on his factors. His wobbly body just begs to be poked. When he goes for a walk, Ira comes to play by nuking his wobbly belly. 'Oh, Nyooop!?'
note: Nyoppurin (spelling from the key item Nyoppurin's Pudding). kakugeki rendered 'nuke' (the strongest attack spell; no English spell name found in the filled data). 'factors' as in Elm3.

en: A Demon Duke. Once, in a Wasteland, nuke after nuke made an Ultimate Mana Source. The magic seemed set to scatter, but suddenly shrank, birthing a huge True Crystal and a demon girl. Childish yet cruel, her peerless magic destroys till all life kneels.
note: Ira. 'kneels at her feet' shortened to 'kneels'. True Crystal as in the key item Ira's True Crystal.

en: A Demon Duke. Head of the noble House Lenzer, revered by the dark knights. He wields the demon axe Baltagias, said to kill any weakling who touches it. Even the Wastelands have laws to keep: to stop Zoze's lawlessness, Dalisiamarte joins hands with Hilde.
note: 'Current head' -> 'Head' for space. 'weakling' = 'one without power'.

en:
Not for loan:
207591.584
Addendum 'Fell Wound'
Kin of Darkness Pel-Dex visits Yanal, Nmachi system; meets King of Ada; both curse gods. Cuts Mixia, god of existence, come to watch: a god's first wound. Names self Demon Duke. Gods' descent in flesh unwise.
note: Light Fiend. Restricted-archive entry in clipped log style (Elm3 'Not for loan:' layout; the record number replaces '------.---'). Yanal, Nmachi: new names. Mixia, King of Ada: Elm3 spellings.

en:
Not for loan:
------.---
'Hevayur'
Hevayur promoted from library staff to deputy librarian on Void's recommendation. That makes three deputies, but only Hevayur has a god's recommendation. Is the next librarian settled?
note: Proto Regiem. raiburarian = library staff, shisho dairi = deputy librarian (Elm3), shisho = librarian (Elm3 uses 'librarian' for both raiburarian and shisho; split here so the promotion reads).

en:
Not for loan:
605213.203
'A Void Axis Appears'
Void Axis seen in Kuus, Mashitra system. Took sibling form, roamed lands; as in past reports, lacking resistance, bodies crumbled. Deemed harmless, but Grand Chancellor neared it in a New Land. Watch.
note: Ordmystica. kyosuuki = Void Axis (Elm3). Kuus, Mashitra: new names. The siblings are Antiworld (row 356). 'Deemed harmless' = judged no problem if left alone.

en:
Not for loan:
000023.006
'Apasha's Atonement Stone'
Apasha, first god of Dark Oblivion, laid the Path of Souls; a hidden flaw spread to all lands since the Primal Soil. Too late. Grief-mad, Apasha became a memorial for undying souls. Fix left to heirs.
note: Dina. gensho no tsuchi = the Primal Soil (Elm3 'the primordial earth'). 'became a memorial for undying souls' = began gathering the souls that cannot be destroyed, itself as their memorial. 'Fix left to successors' = entrusted the hope of a repair to its successors.

en:
Not for loan:
580034.115
Addendum 'Kin of Darkness Strife'
At Arion Dafa, Demon Duke Shantiba falls to Animacie and Dromea's scheme; power sapped, wanders. Her threat thus ends. But her demon cat licked the witch's blood, mutated by grudge: new threat.
note: Potrif. Arion Dafa, Shantiba: new names. kushikumo ('as it happens') rendered 'thus'. The cat is Emperor Harold (row 351); 'her' / 'the witch' = Shantiba (row 351 calls the owner kanojo).

en:
Not for loan:
------.---
'Void Named Chief God'
Long-rumored Void becomes god of space. Void's scenario for creating the Eld: perfect, in a word. With Void as chief, the six gods take the first step to glory and victory. First: sorting out the lands.
note: Meraden. 'chief' = shuseki (the script calls Void 'chief god').

en:
Not for loan:
714729.301
'Bone Dragon's Deicide'
Bone Demon Dragon learns why its land fell; rages. Word it will cross the Horizon to slay a god shakes the Wastes; Divine Realm quakes; System oddly idle. War past forecast opens. Target: Ahadaram's head.
note: Wemricht. Compressed: 'on the Horizon, hard to enter and impossible to escape,' dropped; 'the System looking on, a great mystery' -> 'System oddly idle'. Bone Demon Dragon (kotsumaryuu): new term. System, Divine Realm, Horizon, Ahadaram: Elm3.

en:
Not for loan:
------.---
'The One Called Grand Chancellor'
Conduct of the dark world's Grand Chancellor not to be ignored. Meets many Kin of Darkness, gains much lore; knowing too much is most displeasing. Their words stir the lands. Capture: grand escape.
note: Shining Tusk. 'Their' = the Grand Chancellor (neutral in this entry). 'Capture: a grand escape' = attempts to capture ended in a great escape.

en:
Not for loan:
714729.301
'Urnas Rade'
This Zefkaka has a very bad attitude.
note: Entropha. Urnas Rade form as in the script (slice 065).

en: Cheerful and jolly, a Devilish woman who guzzles drinks while laughing with her customers. Jolly but careless, she misses the little details. That causes some blunders, but apparently a good night's sleep is enough for her to forget anything unpleasant.
note: Berte. Source: 'Devilish woman' (glossary has no gender for Berte; this is evidence: female).

en: A girl who makes her living from the inn her parents left her. It's the only link left to them, so she works as hard as she can to keep it. Maybe that's why she's strict about money, and spends her days let down by adventurers who sleep in the stables.
note: Rosetta.

en: The sharp Director of Administration, a minister in effect. Costo's family has long advised the Bistel royals, and is respected beyond Bistel. But he has one grave flaw: as a noble, he has no idea what things cost. Hence his demotion to the item shop.
note: Costo. gyousei kyokuchou = Director of Administration (glossary question Finance Minister vs Administration Bureau still open). Source uses kare (he) for Costo. 'item shop' = douguya (the Kernel Shop).

en: A priest at the Temple of Orses who heals the illnesses of adventurers and ordinary folk, and gives them advice. He shows understanding toward all things, and listens from the other person's point of view.
note: Bishop Saines (row name: Saines shinpu). shinpu = priest (male), so 'he'.

en: Orphaned by an epidemic as a child, she was taken in by Saines. On a trip to a nearby town, a spirit drifted up to Saines, who heard its grief at becoming a soul of the in-between and purified it. Moved, she took an interest in laying spirits to rest.
note: Sigret (female per glossary).

en: The young Queen of Bistel. For generations the Bistel royal family has held the highest authority as priests of Fiona, the Earth Goddess, and only she can hear Fiona's words directly, as oracles. Off duty, Ragnastia is rather easygoing.
note: Ragnastia. 'Off duty' = su no (her true self, out of her role).

en: A clerk who works at the Bistel Training Hall. Whenever she spots adventurers, she eagerly calls out to them. She walks the town so diligently that there's hardly anyone in Bistel who doesn't know her face.
note: Miria. Source uses kanojo (she); glossary had Miria's gender as unknown.

en: A Dragonfolk Lord who raises heroes. Finding a crowd, Rondelgius takes the most visible spot, and any passing adventurer who seems "the one!" gets an impossible task. Special talent: weaving through crowds to a target without once looking away.
note: Rondelgius. No pronoun (source has none). Dragonfolk as in the script; Lord = the class name kunshu.

en: A bard who wanders from land to land. The breezy looks give a frivolous, flashy impression, but the passion for song and the dedication to studying it are the real thing. Special talent: playing any song after hearing it just once.
note: Haleorat. No pronoun (no gender in source or glossary).

en: Head of House Barnefon, one of two surviving Great Houses of Isfald. The Three Houses are of royal blood and take the throne if the line dies out. The third plotted to kill the royals and was purged by the people. He's carefree, caring only for antiques.
note: Lord Volms. Source uses kare (he). gosanke = the (Three) Great Houses; Barnefon: new name. 'caring only for antiques' = interested in nothing but collecting antique art.

en: A scatterbrained, clumsy fairy who ran a small bazaar in the forest, then, wanting more, came all the way to Isfald. But trade that worked in the forest draws no notice in the city: a real problem. The stock is all unusual, so alchemists like the shop.
note: Lunea: no pronoun (source has none).

en: First Princess of Isfald. Elves grow worldly with politics and money after long in a city, but at heart Leafa stays pure, which makes her a bit of a nuisance to her father the king and his circle. Kept from politics, she wants people who'll do her bidding.
note: Princess Leafa. Compressed: 'unhappy at being kept away from politics' -> 'Kept from politics'.

en: A Yotel Wharf auntie with an only son, Gregorio. She's forever worrying whether Gregorio is bothering people, whether he'll ever stand on his own two feet, and so on. The more trouble a child is, the dearer they are, as the saying goes.
note: Armitt.

en: An old man whose every catch gets snatched by Muse. He used to cheer aloud at every fish he landed, but now, wary of Muse, he tries to make himself unnoticeable. For all his efforts, though, Muse still swipes them.
note: Benef. ojiisan = old man (male).

en: Benef, his youthful strength restored. Now there's no fish he can't catch. Every fish will dance to the tune of his rod.
note: Super Benef.

en: A wandering Werebeast girl who turned up in this port town a few years ago. When Benef, on a whim, fed the starving Muse a fish, she thought, "This geezer's useful, nya! Stick with him for all-you-can-eat fish, nya!" She's chased his fish ever since.
note: Muse (nya as in the script).

en: Muse is an avatar of the Edumo. A Senior is allowed some free action. Long ago it came to this land to eat it all, but agreed to wait when asked by Fiona and the King of Bistel of the day. When starving, Muse turns back into the Edumo and hunts the land.
note: Super Muse. shinia = Senior (as in Edumo Senior, glossary).

en: Owner of a shady antique shop in Saimar. Highly resistant to cursed goods: your average ill-omened item won't make Bilente flinch. Walmitt and the other Saimar merchants have secretly put up a bounty: '1,000,000 GP to whoever can startle Bilente.'
note: Bilente: no pronoun.

en: The head of merchants is a Chief Merchant, and the head of the Chief Merchants is the Grand Merchant, a post they elect. Walmitt is already in a third term. It's time to raise a successor, but there's no one Walmitt can trust with it.
note: Walmitt: no pronoun. Chief Merchant / Grand Merchant per glossary.

en: A Gandra Mine alchemist who lives by smithing and alchemy. A Rubenburg graduate, same year as Vice Principal Kathleen, but skipped dull classes like Ancient Language and was held back twice or so. Once hit on Jera and came back white as a sheet, they say.
note: Tarmeet: no pronoun here; row 390 refers to Tarmeet with kare (male).

en: A man who's simply in the way. Why, of all places, does he hang around the floor that handles food? He's loathed in the Canteen, and it can't be helped. Nobody can stand someone retching right beside them during a nice break from work.
note: Gary. kyuujiba = the Canteen (Elm3 HELP_TEXT).

en: A little cook who works in the Canteen. Tris was made by Tarmeet and is packed with his obsessions about the ideal magic puppet, which makes Tris a bit inflexible at times. In spare moments, Tris loves baking sweets and taking them to Jeratan to play.
note: Tris: no pronoun. 'his' = Tarmeet (source kare no risou).

en: Supposedly the one woman at Gandra Mine. Jera ran the store normally at first, but after dressing up for an event, something awoke. Insiders smirk when a newcomer makes eyes at Jera. Jera truly seeks love, so smiles wryly each time the truth comes out.
note: Source implies Jera is a man in women's clothes (kouitten rashii 'supposedly the only woman', kasou 'dressed up', sujou ga bareru 'true identity found out'; row 388: Tarmeet hit on Jera and came back pale). Kept as hints, no pronouns. Glossary lists Jera as female: check.

en: Mascot of Jera's General Store. Tarmeet built it in Jera's likeness, and Jera remodeled it. At first it was meant to be just a doll, so it was hung from a pillar, and the habit seems to have stuck. It's adorable flailing its arms and legs while hanging.
note: Jeratan ('it': a doll / magic puppet).

en: The man who runs Gandra Mine. Stubborn, he chews people out without hearing them, but his thinking and his skills are sound, so he's well regarded.
note: Garian.

en: An old fairy over 900 years of age. Quasimon has lost the old liveliness, and just sits plopped in the plaza. Quasimon has become a famous sight of Harjiradam, but what does Quasimon think of that?
note: Quasimon: no pronoun.

en: A shrine maiden who prays for the peace of the land, now 87. No regrets over a life of prayer, but always wonders, "What if I'd lived differently..." Loves the fan-tossing game; told of it, Namina had a flash: play it with Quasimon. One more joy!
note: Kine: no pronoun. tousenkyou = the fan-tossing game (Elm3); Quasimon is to be the target. 'One more joy!' = and so Kine gained one more pleasure. 'without cease' dropped for space.

en: A girl who adores Archbishop Mersenne. When she was small, Mersenne came to her village with Semnadoc's teachings. Moved by them, Namina came here, but lately she seems to have forgotten them a little. At such a sensitive age, maybe it can't be helped.
note: Namina. Source: shoujo (girl); glossary says the script has not settled the gender.

en: A go-getter merchant of Semnadoc, always chasing what's new. She's eager to sell herself to other towns, but among merchants she's already well known as Semnadoc's go-getter girl. She wants to open a branch, and for a while Lunea's Shop was a candidate.
note: Caron. Source calls Caron shoujo (girl); glossary had no explicit gender.

en: Semnadoc's young Archbishop, who as a child saw the giant goddess statue, fell for it, swore to become Archbishop, and did. Each morning at the temple door he looks up, cries "O great, fair Semnadoc, thanks for your mercy today too!!" 10 times, and weeps.
note: Mersenne. Source: kyodai megami-zou, a giant GODDESS statue of Semnadoc (glossary leaves Semnadoc's gender open). Compressed: 'it is his daily routine' carried by 'Each morning'; 'tears of rapture' -> 'weeps'.

en: A spacey Gnome Priest with a drawn-out way of talking. Gives career guidance at Rubenburg. Bad kids get a "That's no goood~?" lecture until they turn good. Sometimes freezes mid-smile. It may startle you at first, but it's Professor Harmoni, so it's fine.
note: Harmoni: no pronoun.

en: Gives career guidance in evil, with Professor Harmoni. Brilliant, sensible, reliable: the opposite of Professor Harmoni in every way, so some students whisper Warmoni is a doppelganger summoned by arcane arts. One tried an ambush interview. No word since.
note: Warmoni: no pronoun. 'One tried' = source 'some student reportedly tried'; 'no word since' = nothing has been heard of it since. 'career guidance in evil' keeps the Haru/Waru pun.

en: A girl gifted for magic. Her rare talent took her out of the Training Hall to study at Rubenburg. Stubborn, a sore loser and a hard worker, she went on to graduate top of her class. Her dream is to use her power for the land and its people.
note: Soara.

en: A Skunk Girl in a fix, kicked out of job after job because she gasses everywhere she goes. She came here thinking a church would surely give her work.
note: Analis.

en: A gentle, meek rich boy, trying hard to act grown-up so he can lead the dark world. He leans on his wet nurse Gurtia for everything. Never doubting anyone, he's unlikely to learn her true feelings. He swings the "demon sword baltagias" his uncle gave him.
note: Mirco. The sword name is in childish hiragana in the source; lowercase 'baltagias' mirrors that.

en: A bully. A true sadist. Her position has her obey Mirco, but she sees it as training the hopeless boy. If his life is truly at risk, she'll save him, grudgingly. Seeing him cry is her hobby and greatest joy. Mirco never sees he's bullied, and adores her.
note: Gurtia.

en: A sincere, kind elder devoted to House Lenzer, doting on Mirco like a grandchild. Mirco's lack of strength and leadership is a worry, but Hess trusts he'll be a fine head one day. No match for the young women, Hess panics when they make Mirco cry.
note: Hess: no pronoun (glossary keeps Hess's gender open; roujin = 'elder').

en: Once fought Dalisiamarte alone and lost utterly. Conceding, Zephal tried to die by the blade on the spot, but Dalisiamarte liked that; over drinks they bonded, and Zephal swore his soul's obedience. Now a top Lenzer swordsman, he too despairs of Mirco.
note: Zephal (male per glossary). jijin = take one's own life by the blade.

en: A tomboyish harpy who lived near House Lenzer and often teased Mirco. One day Gurtia caught her at it, but far from scolding her, gave her a lecture on how to enjoy Mirco. Since then she's looked up to Gurtia as her master (in Mirco-teasing).
note: Elpina.

en: A custom griffon made for Mirco, with no intention of carrying the green Mirco and no time for him. Mirco once jumped the sleeping Zapper to ride by force, was caught halfway and beaten to a pulp. It wasn't about the ride: he was angry at the cowardly act.
note: Zapper. Source uses kare (he); glossary had Zapper's gender as not stated.

en: A Raizam, worn out and frazzled underground beneath the desert. Somehow, the Blanc Desert seems to be an uncomfortable place for him. Is there something there he can't stand?
note: Raizam-1. Source uses kare (he) for Raizam; glossary had no explicit gender.

note: Column header / template row.

note: Column header / template row.
Column header with the designer's 16-character ruler (layout only). debug?

en: !Roma
note: Preset character nickname, same pattern as !Priest, !Ranger (Roma = class name in the filled data).

en:
Alchemy Item No. 1.
Air Fruit. This lets you breathe even underwater. With it, you can even explore underwater dungeons.

>Frozen Elven Iron x Vectreim
>Vectreim x Tri-Layer Orat
note: Recipe lines keep the source's '>' marks. The source writes the first material without 'iron' (truncated); full item name used. Vectreim = ITEM name (glossary script term: Vectraim; check).
Designer's line-number ruler for the 8-line description box (layout only).

en:
Alchemy Item No. 2.
Angel's Window. When you enter a cave, it shows your surroundings in a little window. Make one if you don't want to get lost.

>Dvel Soft Steel x Frozen Elven Iron

Alchemy Item No. 3.
Rock Counter. It tells you how many stone blocks are on the floor. If a square on your map just won't fill in, it may be stone, so try it.

>Dvel Soft Steel x Tri-Layer Orat
>Vectreim x Mazurite

Alchemy Item No. 4.
Dove Bell. This drives off the enemies lying in wait on the floor. Try it when you want to breeze through.

>Frozen Elven Iron x Mazurite
>Mazurite x Tri-Layer Orat

Alchemy Item No. 5.
Crow Bell. Some monsters guard certain rooms. Once beaten, they stay gone until you change floors, but ring this and they return.

>Dvel Soft Steel x Vectreim
>Tri-Layer Orat x Milstone

Alchemy Item No. 6.
Sheep's Brush. It marks enemies lying in wait when you view the map. Just carrying it helps, so make at least one.

>Dvel Soft Steel x Mazurite
>Frozen Elven Iron x Milstone

Alchemy Item No. 7.
Bone Slippers. If your party is wiped out, these send you home automatically. As corpses, of course.

>Dvel Soft Steel x Milstone
>Frozen Elven Iron x Tri-Layer Orat
note: 'home' = kokyou (hometown); Elm3 'back to town'.

en:
Alchemy Item No. 8.
Death Pinwheel. When enemies appear, it tells you their level. If the gap is too wide, knowing when to run matters too!

>Vectreim x Milstone
note: 'knowing when to run matters too' = nigeru no mo daiji da zo (running away is important too).
